tasks.short: Interpret allergy tests against the clinical picture

steps.what: Read diagnostic test results with specimen dates, units, reference ranges and relevant clinical history
Interpret diagnostic test results and make appropriate differential diagnoses, including discordant findings and uncertainty

tasks.design: Configure a native result view in {OPS_SYSTEM} with dates, units and links to the original laboratory reports. The allergist checks the sources and interprets the differential diagnosis; the view does not make diagnostic decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results and clinical context can require several record views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native result filtering and chronological views can reduce navigation.
tasks.still_hard: A test finding is not sufficient on its own to establish the cause of symptoms.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret conflicting findings against the individual clinical picture.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical record systems can display source results by date without automating differential diagnosis.

assumptions: Boundary is result interpretation and diagnostic reasoning; document authoring is not repeated here because medical-history documentation is separately modeled. No clinical order or send is performed.

OPS_SYSTEM denotes the clinical record. Laboratory staff supply patient and specimen identifiers, analyte, value, units, reference range and date; existing clinicians supply history. Missing or mismatched fields require manual source reading within s1, not fabricated normalization.
Test native views before custom integration. Shares and remaining time are provisional work scenarios, not measured baselines; runtime itself earns no saving.
Gross 5 points minus 0.5 upkeep gives 4.5 net; actual diagnostic reasoning remains fully retained.
research_questions: Does the view reduce navigation while exposing discordant and missing results?

already_counted.description: Verify source results and patient context

incremental.description: Check result-view mappings after laboratory changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero for a sufficient existing view; up to 3% net when navigation improves less than the central 4.5% scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Obtain and clarify the patient's medical history and reconcile relevant existing records
Compose the medical-history note from the actual clarified history
outputs: medical-history note draft with source references

loop.purpose: Organize the clinician's actual history into a note
loop.input: Clinician dictation and selected existing history
loop.output: Draft preserving attribution, chronology and uncertainty
loop.check: Allergist compares every history statement to sources, including negation, medication names, exposures and dates
loop.stop: One corrected redraft, then manual editing; omit unsupported details
loop.why_not_simpler: Native verbatim dictation is tried first; narrative organization may require reading meaning

steps.what: Correct and authenticate the completed medical-history note against the actual account
inputs: medical-history note draft with source references

steps.what: Save the authenticated final history to the same patient record

tasks.design: Test native dictation and history templates in {OPS_SYSTEM} before a bounded narrative-drafting loop. The allergist supplies the actual history, corrects and authenticates the final note, then saves that version; no ambient recording is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative composition competes with listening and clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Dictation and bounded drafting can organize actual clinician-supplied content.
tasks.still_hard: Preserve denied symptoms, uncertain recollections and who reported each fact.
tasks.human_edge: Clarify the account and accept responsibility for the clinical record.

ambition.what: No additional service funded before measuring the documentation change.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10; clinical governance, access and applicable consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: dictation and narrative drafting can assist medical notes but require clinician correction and authentication.

assumptions: Boundary includes acquiring and documenting the history; dictation and clarification time is explicitly retained in s1, not supplied by an uncounted producer.

OPS_SYSTEM is the clinical record. The clinician supplies patient identity, actual reported history, attribution and uncertainty; selected existing entries retain authors and dates. If dictation capture fails, manual note authoring returns.
Native dictation first; use the loop only if it improves total correction-inclusive time. Shares are unmeasured scenarios. Existing record authentication is not an invented approval meeting.
Same-system save takes approximately no time and receives 1% fully retained. Gross 14 minus upkeep 1 yields 13% net.
unknowns: Actual dictation, writing and correction times
research_questions: Does source-grounded drafting reduce total note effort without changing negation or attribution?

already_counted.description: Draft correction and final clinical authentication

incremental.description: Review recurring note defects and maintain the history template

approvals.approved_version: authenticated final history from s3; edits invalidate authentication

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native dictation is already sufficient; up to 10% when correction reduces the central 13% net benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop an individualized allergy treatment plan

steps.what: Review the patient's clinical data and current treatment context
Discuss patient preferences and explain the relevant risks and benefits of possible therapies
outputs: clarified preferences and discussed treatment choices

steps.what: Select the individualized treatment plan using clinical data, patient preferences and therapy risks and benefits
inputs: clarified preferences and discussed treatment choices

steps.what: Write the selected plan in the patient record's treatment-plan fields
Check the complete plan reflects the selected treatment and patient preferences and authenticate the final version
Save the authenticated plan within the same clinical record

tasks.design: Configure the existing treatment-plan template in {OPS_SYSTEM} to reuse clinician-selected sections without generating treatment decisions. The allergist supplies patient-specific choices and preferences, checks the completed plan and saves the authenticated version.
tasks.previous_blocker: A blank plan requires repeated formatting and standard section entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can supply headings and clinician-selected standard text.
tasks.still_hard: A standard section may be inappropriate to the individual's risks or preferences.
tasks.human_edge: Choose and explain an individualized course of care.

ambition.what: Do not expand clinical throughput from an unmeasured template change.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native clinical templates can reduce repeated plan formatting while leaving treatment choice with the clinician.

assumptions: Boundary ends at the individualized plan. Prescriptions, orders and patient sends are separate actions and receive no saving here.

OPS_SYSTEM is the clinical record. The allergist supplies the actual selected treatment, relevant patient preferences and risk considerations through s1-s3. Templates contain no automatically selected therapy or unverified default patient facts.
Native templates first; clinician edits remain counted in s4 and final authentication in s5. These are clinical plan-writing and authentication, not a newly imposed sign-off process.

Shares are provisional scenarios; gross 5 minus 0.5 upkeep leaves 4.5 net. Same-system save has 1% fully retained and contributes no saving. Resolve overlap with clinical-history documentation at roll-up.
unknowns: Whether the current plan template already suffices
research_questions: Does a template reduce repeated formatting without carrying inappropriate default treatments?

already_counted.description: Patient-specific plan entry and final clinical authentication

incremental.description: Maintain template sections under clinical governance

approvals.approved_version: authenticated final plan from s5; any edit requires renewed check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if templates are already efficient; up to 3% where the measured reduction is smaller than the central 4.5% net scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Weigh therapy risks and benefits for the patient

steps.what: Consult relevant patient data and current approved therapy references
outputs: source-checked therapy information and patient risk factors

steps.what: Assess the risks and benefits of therapies for allergic and immunologic disorders in this patient's circumstances
inputs: source-checked therapy information and patient risk factors

tasks.design: Use approved reference bookmarks in {DOCS} beside the patient data in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Reduce reference navigation only; the allergist weighs benefits, uncertainty and individual risks without a generated treatment recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating the applicable reference can interrupt clinical reasoning.
tasks.enabler_now: Native indexed references and bookmarks can reduce searching.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence may be incomplete for this patient's circumstances.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when generic evidence does not fit the patient.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: approved-reference indexing can assist retrieval without deciding a patient's therapy risk-benefit balance.

assumptions: Boundary is assessing therapies, not prescribing, sending advice or writing a treatment plan. No separate assessment document is established or assigned baseline time.
Clinical staff already author patient data; reference owners supply approved documents with title, version and scope. Missing references trigger manual search within s1, not generated claims.

Native bookmarks and indexing first. Shares and retrieval reduction are provisional scenarios; gross 3 minus 0.5 upkeep leaves 2.5 net. Resolve overlapping clinical review with plan development at roll-up.
unknowns: Which references have a maintained approval process
research_questions: Can native indexing reduce source retrieval without directing treatment choice?

already_counted.description: Read and verify retrieved reference material

incremental.description: Check bookmarked references for superseded versions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if current retrieval is already immediate; up to 1.5% where retrieval improves less than the central 2.5% net scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical diagnosis and treatment authority stay with the allergist; source navigation and documentation receive limited assistance.
skills_to_grow: Check clinical narrative attribution and negation
Maintain native clinical templates and source-linked views
role.ambitious_version: A clearer source-grounded record without transferring diagnosis or therapy decisions to software.
